sourceSentences: Hecarim gains bonus attack damage equal to a percentage of his bonus movement speed.
If this damages an enemy, Hecarim gains a stack of Rampage for 8 seconds, refreshing on subsequent damage and stacking up to 3 times.
Stacks expire one by one every 1 second when the duration ends.

While active, Hecarim gains bonus armor and bonus magic resistance and is healed for 25% of the post-mitigation damage dealt to enemies within the area from all sources, halved for damage dealt by allies. The healing is capped against minions and monsters.
Hecarim's next basic attack is replaced by a Devastating Charge, empowering it to gain range and cause him to dash in the target's direction
Hecarim knocks them back, though not through terrain
Hecarim can cast any of his champion abilities during the dash. Devastating Charge's duration is paused during Onslaught of Shadows.
Onslaught of Shadows will interrupt the dash.
If the target does not remain nearby during the dash, Devastating Charge's effect will not be consumed.
The dash does not follow targets. The target's position at the time of the enhanced attack is the direction Hecarim will leap to.
Displacement immunity will not resist the application of the stun.
Upon arrival, he fears nearby enemies for 0.75 to 1.5 seconds depending on distance traveled.
The wave of spectral riders travels independently of Hecarim and will always charge at the same distance.
Only the spectral riders deal damage to enemies they pierce, Hecarim only dashes and fears enemies at the end of it.
For combos, start with E to gain movement speed, then when moving towards the target, use W into your attack and Q. From here, simply keep spamming away with auto attacks and Qs.
And a good engage combo is start with ultimate into W and follow up with E and Q.
Each stack makes the next Q deal bonus damage and also reduces the cool down of it by a good chunk.
before you gank, you want to make sure you keep the stacks.
when you E in, before you hit the guy, try to get as high speed as you can and then hit him with a Q.
you're going to E in, right? And then you're going to R him. And I still have the E charge, so you can knock him back.
the farther away it is, he does more of a fear.
That's something that people don't realize is you can just smite when you're in your W
